```{r, setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(safeAI)
```

## One mathematical engine, three interpretations

The functions `rga()`, `rgr()`, and `rge()` use the same univariate rank-graduation comparison but apply it to different pairs of vectors:

- accuracy: observed outcomes versus predictions;
- robustness: baseline predictions versus predictions generated under a robustness scenario;
- explainability: full-model predictions versus reduced-model predictions.

```{r}
y <- c(2, 3, 5, 7)
yhat <- c(3, 7, 2, 5)
rga(y, yhat)
```

## Tie handling

Ranking values are rounded to six decimal places by default. When ranking values are tied, their corresponding reference values are replaced by their mean before the concordance ordering is formed.

```{r}
rga(1:5, rep(1, 5))
```

## Robustness

The analyst supplies both prediction vectors. The second vector may be generated by changing the data, model, inputs, parameters, or another part of the predictive workflow.

```{r}
pred_baseline <- c(0.12, 0.31, 0.55, 0.73, 0.91)
pred_stressed <- c(0.15, 0.28, 0.58, 0.70, 0.88)
rgr(pred_baseline, pred_stressed)
```

## Explainability

```{r}
pred_full <- c(0.1, 0.3, 0.7, 0.9)
pred_reduced <- c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8)
rge(pred_full, pred_reduced)
```

## Ordinal outcomes

Ordered factors are accepted directly as reference outcomes.

```{r}
actual <- ordered(
  c("low", "medium", "high", "medium"),
  levels = c("low", "medium", "high")
)
predicted_score <- c(1.1, 2.2, 2.8, 1.9)
rga(actual, predicted_score)
```

## Underlying curves

```{r}
rg_curves(y, yhat)
```
